obtained.how: the human's fetch of the publisher's first-page preview image (p. 149 only, a 644 × 951 GIF), converted to a one-page PDF for indexing; no text layer, read on the image. Pages 150-151 (the data) were not obtainable

bibliography.checked_against: Crossref and the article's first page (p. 149)
bibliography.note: Kendall Warner, Maine Department of Inland Fisheries and Game, Bangor; 'Spring Food of Chain Pickerel (Esox niger) in Maine Lakes'; Transactions of the American Fisheries Society 102(1): 149-151 (1973), a Short Paper and Note; matches the entry

claims.claim: Warner (1973) is a Maine study of spring chain pickerel food, seen only in its introduction (data pages not seen)
claims.location: p. 149 (the only page seen), right column
claims.quote: document food habits of chain pickerel collected from Maine lakes in the spring
claims.conditions: fish collected over about 1 month from ice-out, in conjunction with a study of pickerel predation on stocked salmonids (Warner et al. 1968)
claims.note: pp. 150-151 are still unseen, so no diet value can be taken from it; the paper's statement that only the introduction has been seen remains true

claims.claim: the one Maine study of spring pickerel food
claims.note: p. 149 names no other spring study, but cites three Maine pickerel food-habits studies of unstated season (Cooper 1941; Fuller & Cooper 1946; Barr 1962); 'the one' is the project's claim and cannot be checked from this page

claims.claim: Apart from Warner (1973), the only Maine diet-composition data for adults of either piscivore are Cooper's (1941)
claims.source_value: Warner's introduction names two more Maine pickerel food-habits studies besides Cooper (1941): Fuller and Cooper (1946) and Barr (1962); and Warner et al. (1968) on pickerel predation on newly stocked salmonids in Maine
claims.quote: studied by Cooper (1941), Fuller and Cooper (1946), and Barr (1962)
claims.note: the full sentence begins 'Food habits of pickerel in Maine waters have been'. Whether Fuller & Cooper 1946 and Barr 1962 report adult diet composition is not known from this page; the rewrite should either find them or say 'the only one found'.

notes: The p. 149 GIF (docs/research_notes/fetched/tafs_102_1_tafs0149.pdf.gif) is OUP's first-page preview; its upper part ends a cui-ui paper. Warner's introduction also cites Kendall 1917, Hunter & Rankin 1939, Foote & Blake 1945 and Wich 1958 (fish the major food except for very young pickerel, which eat insects and crustaceans; large pickerel take frogs, snakes and almost any moving object of proper size).
